question: Should the experimental Claws lifecycle own globally named MCP server entries and remove unchanged owned entries during Claw cleanup?
rationale: The open RFC proposes this boundary, but accepting a new shared-config owner and destructive cleanup contract requires maintainer intent beyond implementation correctness.

options.title: Approve guarded ownership
options.body: Accept the RFC boundary with explicit consent, create-only writes, compare-before-remove, and blocked cleanup for modified or ambiguous entries.

options.title: Keep MCP operator-owned
options.body: Limit Claws to validation and export while leaving global MCP installation and removal to operators or another setup surface.

options.title: Pause the MCP slice
options.body: Keep this draft unlanded until the full Claws RFC and preceding stack establish an accepted lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded ownership
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC boundary with explicit consent, create-only writes, compare-before-remove, and blocked cleanup for modified or ambiguous entries.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history identifies this person as the introducer of the shared MCP writer whose ownership contract would be extended.
